name: stri_endswith_coll
title: Determine if the Start or End of a String Matches a Pattern

origin.description: Report whether a collation pattern ends at a code-point index.
origin.usage: stri_endswith_coll(str, pattern, to = -1L, negate = FALSE, ..., opts_collator = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of collation patterns. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: 1-based code-point index where the match must end. -1 is the end of the string.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, report strings that do not match.

arguments.name: opts_collator
arguments.text: NULL, or a named list from stri_opts_collator. Only supplied settings are stored.
Collator settings passed to stri_opts_collator: locale, strength, alternate_shifted, french, uppercase_first, case_level, normalization, normalisation, numeric.

origin.details: Inputs are recycled to the longer length. A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, is missing. Matching uses ICU StringSearch. The next match starts after the previous one, so the pattern can be longer than the text it consumes: at strength 1 in German, ss matches each ß on its own. opts_collator is a dict of only the settings that were passed. The normalization setting is the key normalization. A keyword normalisation is stored under that key. Locale C is en_US_POSIX. Strength 1 is primary and strength 4 is quaternary. Numeric collation makes the searcher raise U_UNSUPPORTED_ERROR. Positions from the locate functions are 1-based inclusive code points.
origin.value: A logical vector. A missing result is NA.
origin.example:
hit <- stri_endswith_coll("x\u00df", "ss", strength = 1, locale = "de")
cat(paste0('stri_endswith_coll("xß", "ss", strength=1, locale="de") returns ', if (isTRUE(hit)) "TRUE" else "FALSE", '.\n'))

translation.description: Report whether a collation pattern ends at a code-point index.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Collation pattern, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: 1-based code-point index where the match must end. -1 is the end of the string.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, report strings that do not match.

arguments.name: opts_collator
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the settings that were passed. The normalization key is normalization.

arguments.name: collator
arguments.text: Keyword settings merged by stri_opts_collator. normalisation is stored as normalization.

translation.details: Inputs are recycled to the longer length. A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, is missing. Matching uses ICU StringSearch. The next match starts after the previous one, so the pattern can be longer than the text it consumes: at strength 1 in German, ss matches each ß on its own. opts_collator is a dict of only the settings that were passed. The normalization setting is the key normalization. A keyword normalisation is stored under that key. Locale C is en_US_POSIX. Strength 1 is primary and strength 4 is quaternary. Numeric collation makes the searcher raise U_UNSUPPORTED_ERROR. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. from_ is R's from.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.coll import stri_endswith_coll
hit = stri_endswith_coll("xß", "ss", strength=1, locale="de")[0]
word = "TRUE" if hit else "FALSE"
print(f'stri_endswith_coll("xß", "ss", strength=1, locale="de") returns {word}.')
